_comment: The thrown bomb (docs/plan-prototype-projectile.md D1/D6, P1): the entity a `projectile` cooldown places a few units ahead of its caster. It is a MOB because a mob is already everything a projectile needs to be - it registers with the SkillSystem, it carries a loadout, it has a TTL and it removes cleanly - so the prototype adds no entity kind. role structure = no AI, no chase, no aggro sensor; it lands where it is thrown and stays. BODY IS THE TOTEM RECIPE VERBATIM: collisionLayer 160 (Player 128 + Viewport 32) is the player-layer trick, so a hostile mob's aura can reach it and mobs will aggro onto it (§5 calls that free decoy a FEATURE to be judged, not a bug), and collisionMask 16 (Border only) means nothing pushes it and it pushes nothing. ⭐ ITS DETONATION IS ITS OWN LOADOUT (D4): BombBurst sits in a cooldown slot, the spawn site holds that cooldown down for the throw's armTicks, and the SHIPPED mob auto-fire path - which fires a ready cooldown every tick and consumes it only on a hit - is then the entire trigger. Armed, waits, bangs when someone wanders in. No detonation machinery was written. baseMaxHealth 9999 is D6's authored split at prototype fidelity, not a pool anybody is meant to read: a player-thrown bomb must survive its own few seconds, and the P3 boss bomb will author a small pool so players can burst it down before it pops. It costs nothing to make it unkillable and a defuse mechanic is deferred. It pays for the pool with speed 0, which is what keeps it inside the archetype guardrail. ⛑ entityType NpcPlaceholder is DELIBERATE placeholder art, the PortalHome call again: a bespoke EntityType costs a wire enum value that can never be reclaimed plus an exhaustive client Record entry, and the prototype earns its own sprite only if it merges. xpFactor 0 keeps it off the nameplate and the XP path - a thrown bomb is not prey. curveLevel 1 because the scaling comes from owner binding, like every summon. ALL VALUES [PLACEHOLDER], per the GDD rule.
